items.headline: Colorado ties for No. 1 in national child care scorecard on workforce supports
items.summary: Credential uptake at 72% of the workforce and a $23.4m care-worker tax credit ease hiring cost and turnover for Colorado centers.

items.headline: Child Trends evaluation says Colorado universal preschool needs tougher quality standards
items.summary: Colorado meets only 2 of 10 quality benchmarks; tighter class-size, ratio and credential rules would raise staffing cost per classroom.

items.headline: Colorado counties begin paying CCCAP providers on enrollment, not daily attendance, in August 2026
items.summary: Removes absence-driven revenue leakage — subsidy revenue becomes predictable for Colorado centers starting this month.

items.headline: CDEC adopts new CCCAP rules: financial safeguards plus processes to clear waitlists and lift freezes
items.summary: Creates a path to re-open enrollment where freezes had capped subsidized demand.
